purpose: Explicit, reversible review plan for known Armani canonical-identity collisions. This is a proposal only; it is not an executable migration.
approval_requirements: Verify product identity and concentration against authoritative manufacturer references.
Verify each affected size/variant against an authoritative source or GTIN/MPN.
Inventory all offer mappings and downstream references before moving or retiring any product_id.
Prepare a backup and rollback mapping before any catalog write.
Run the migration validator and end-to-end tests against a copy before review.

cases.diagnosis: Probable incomplete duplicate/legacy parent record, but SH-AUTO-0288 has no declared concentration or variants and must not be silently merged.
cases.proposed_action: Review SH-AUTO-0288 as a possible legacy alias/redirect to SH-AUTO-0018 only after confirming the official identity and finding every reference to SH-AUTO-0288. Preserve the old ID as a redirect/compatibility mapping if the repository supports it.
blocking_questions: Does every existing reference to SH-AUTO-0288 refer specifically to the EDT product?
Are there any non-EDT Acqua di Gio products or historical references represented by this record?

external_check.conclusion: The official catalog distinguishes Acqua di Giò EDT from other concentrations and Profondo. SH-AUTO-0018 is consistent with an EDT identity and declared 50/100/200 ml sizes; SH-AUTO-0288 remains an incomplete generic record. This does not establish that every reference to SH-AUTO-0288 is an EDT reference.

cases.diagnosis: Same normalized brand, canonical name and concentration split across two product IDs. Available records alone do not prove whether the sizes belong to one identity or whether a historical/release distinction is missing.
cases.proposed_action: Do not merge yet. Verify 75 ml and 125 ml with authoritative sources and verify all five variants independently. If they are the same product identity, nominate one canonical product ID, move variants without changing variant IDs, consolidate aliases without losing provenance, and preserve an old-ID redirect/reference map. Correct or validate the SH-0043 canonical image separately.
blocking_questions: Are the 75 ml and 125 ml EDP formats valid for the exact same Profondo release/market?
Which product ID is referenced by persisted offers, scraper mappings, analytics, or external clients?
Does the image currently attached to SH-0043 actually depict the canonical product and size?

external_check.conclusion: Current official sources list Profondo EDP 30/50/100/200 ml and a separate 150 ml refill; they do not list 75 ml or 125 ml on the pages checked. This is insufficient to delete or reassign those variants because older releases/markets remain possible. The SH-0043 image-size mismatch also remains unverified.

rollback_plan: Export and checksum the pre-migration product and variant records plus all references to affected product IDs.
Apply the approved mapping transactionally on a staging copy.
Validate unique product/variant IDs, variant ownership, GTIN/MPN uniqueness, reference integrity, and unchanged unaffected-record counts.
If any validation fails, restore the exact pre-migration snapshot and report the failure without publishing.

dependency_inventory.result: No persisted offer rows, GTINs, MPNs, or store_mappings are present for the four affected product identities/variants in the checked catalog snapshot.

code_reference_search.result: No direct literal references found in the core runtime files checked (backend/catalog_engine.py, backend/product_matcher.py, backend/main.py, and Next Engine repository/matcher/service files).
code_reference_search.caveat: This is not proof that runtime databases, logs, caches, external clients, or dynamically keyed mappings have no references. Full-repository exhaustive code search was not completed.

dependency_inventory.safety_conclusion: The checked catalog snapshot shows no in-catalog offer or retailer mapping dependencies, but that alone is not enough to authorize a merge. Runtime persistence and deployed data still need a read-only inventory before any catalog write.

deployed_runtime_check.finding: A manual GitHub Actions workflow connected to the deployed Fly.io app and opened the SQLite database with mode=ro and PRAGMA query_only=ON. It scanned 18 tables/views and exact-matched the 12 target IDs.
deployed_runtime_check.interpretation: The four product IDs occur in catalog_coverage only in this exact-ID scan; none of the eight target variant IDs were found as exact values in scanned columns. This is not proof of no indirect, serialized, external, or name-based references.
deployed_runtime_check.limitation: The workflow scanned exact ID values, not Armani product names or partial IDs. It did not establish whether catalog_coverage rows are operational dependencies. Do not merge or delete identities on this evidence alone.

store_products.sample_note: 30 rows sampled for name LIKE '%acqua di gio%'; retailer data contains distinct Acqua di Gio EDT 30/50/100 ml, Profondo EDP 30/50 ml, and a PerfumeMarket listing for Profondo EDP 125 ml. Sample includes other family products (Gioia, Profumo, aftershave, deodorant), so substring matches are not sufficient identity evidence.

name_based_reference_scan.interpretation: The production DB contains retailer text and URL references for the Armani family. catalog_coverage rows are operational retailer-search coverage, not evidence of offer mappings. Retailer inventory includes a 125 ml Profondo EDP listing, but this is third-party evidence and does not settle the exact release/market identity. Exact variant IDs still were not found in the earlier scan.
limitations: This audit searched the text 'armani' across columns and then sampled up to 30 rows by broad 'acqua di gio' substring; it is not a complete row-level mapping of every affected product/variant to every retailer offer.
The scan returns a few sample values per column, not all matching retailer records.
No write was made to the deployed database.

profondo_size_reconciliation.interpretation: Production retailer data contains two distinct retailer listings for Profondo EDP 125 ml, with the PerfumeMarket listing carrying SKU 3614272865235. The English PerfumeMarket duplicate has no size_ml value. This is retailer evidence for a 125 ml listing, not manufacturer-authoritative proof and not proof that either catalog variant is correctly mapped to these rows.
limitations: The query returned no 75 ml row.
GTIN and MPN fields were empty for all three returned rows.
The SKU resembles a GTIN-13 format but is stored in sku, not gtin; do not promote it to a verified GTIN without independent validation.
The query is name/size-filtered and capped at 100 rows; it does not establish all possible references or offer-to-variant links.
profondo_size_reconciliation.safety: Read-only connection with SQLite URI mode=ro and PRAGMA query_only=ON; no production data was changed.

follow_up.failure_reason: The new workflow's inline Python command has a quoting SyntaxError before executing its database query; the connection was opened read-only and no database mutation occurred.
follow_up.conclusion: The targeted 125 ml retailer evidence is recorded, but mapping-table schema and exact retailer-to-canonical-variant links remain unverified. Do not merge or migrate either Armani identity collision on current evidence.

findings.store_url_metadata: No matching rows for exact Acqua di Gio Profondo product-name/url criteria or SKU 3614272865235.
findings.store_products: Retailer rows confirm current Profondo EDP 30/50/100 ml listings and several 125 ml EDP listings; at least one retailer listing carries SKU 3614272865235 and GTIN 3614272865235 in a separate retailer record. The deployed database also has Profondo Parfum and refill listings that must not be conflated with Profondo EDP.
findings.parser_errors: Several Deloox and Parfumzentrum EDP product URLs have fetch_status product_parser_not_found despite HTTP 200 and JSON-LD Product presence; this is a separate scraper/parser issue and may prevent size_ml normalization.
findings.catalog_coverage: Search-task records exist for both Profondo canonical IDs, with multiple RETRY/timeouts and mixed FOUND/NOT_FOUND states. These are search coverage tasks, not product-to-variant mappings.

latest_variant_audit.conclusion: The audit is now operational and has surfaced concrete retailer data and parser failures, but no explicit retailer-URL/SKU-to-canonical-variant mapping table is present among the queried tables. The 125 ml format has third-party support; the 75 ml format remains unverified. Do not merge product IDs until parser/size normalization and downstream mapping evidence are resolved.

next_gate.required_action: Reconcile the affected product IDs with exact retailer records by product name, concentration, size_ml, URL, GTIN/MPN and any store mapping columns. Treat catalog_coverage as search-task metadata, not offers. Specifically verify SH-AUTO-0288 versus SH-AUTO-0018 EDT and SH-0043 75/125 ml versus SH-AUTO-0019 50/100/200 ml Profondo EDP. Do not merge until variant-level mappings and any parser failures are resolved.
next_gate.no_mutation_guarantee: Keep production database in mode=ro with PRAGMA query_only=ON. No deploy, no writes to production, no automatic merge.
next_gate.latest_evidence: On commit 36e3c711ef19990c3e05c8a4094f350e63b1f932, the full Next Engine tests passed (run 39947671434) and the read-only runtime SQLite audit passed (run 39947671382). A reviewed, generic GTIN-to-variant registry now maps valid GTIN-13 3614272865235 to SH-0043 / VAR-09a73d0a5594cf49 only when GTIN, size, brand, concentration and product-name checks agree. The live Parfum-Zentrum page parses as 125 ml EDP with that GTIN; the matcher regression now resolves it to the 125 ml variant. The separate 100 ml refill with GTIN 3614273953849 remains unmapped and is not assigned to the regular 100 ml EDP. Deloox direct pages remain HTTP 403 from GitHub-hosted runners, so that parser is not live-verified. No merge, deploy or production DB write. The improved live probe (run 39947864353) now distinguishes discovery failures from verified not-found: Deloox reports unavailable after 9 failed search-page attempts and HTTP 403 on exact pages; Parfum-Zentrum reports partial/unverified broad search while both exact product pages parse. Next Engine tests and the read-only runtime audit both passed on commit b6350f5d3f9b1284e1d487ac6729b3f8e16ace91 (runs 39947864281 and 39947864236).
required_next_steps: Keep SH-0043 and SH-AUTO-0019 as separate product identities; the GTIN registry resolves only the verified 125 ml variant and is not permission to merge or delete either product.
Verify the 75 ml Profondo EDP variant and its exact GTIN independently before assigning it automatically.
Keep the 100 ml refill distinct; add a GTIN mapping only after independently verifying its canonical refill variant.
Diagnose Deloox search/discovery and HTTP 403 separately; do not claim its live parser works until a live response is successfully parsed.
Keep SH-AUTO-0288 versus SH-AUTO-0018 blocked until all references to the generic Acqua di Gio record are classified.

variant_resolution_regression.note: GTIN registry is read-only source-controlled evidence. Exact GTIN alone is not enough: runtime also validates target existence, exact size, brand, concentration, product-name compatibility, and refill status.

runtime_audit_tool.execution: Run against a read-only copy/snapshot of the actual Fly.io persistent SQLite database. Do not deploy this branch merely to run the audit; production deployment remains on main.

parser_reconciliation.change: extract_product_page now accepts already-fetched HTML and parses that response instead of always issuing a second HTTP request; direct callers without HTML retain the legacy fetch path.
parser_reconciliation.reason: The catalog engine already downloads the product page and passes html only when the retailer parser signature supports it. Deloox previously did not accept html, causing a second independent request and potential divergence between the response audited by the catalog engine and the response parsed by the retailer adapter.
parser_reconciliation.limits: This removes the duplicate-fetch failure mode for Deloox. It does not yet prove all existing parser_not_found rows are fixed; ParfumZentrum still requires separate diagnosis, and retailer-to-canonical variant mapping remains unresolved.

parfumzentrum.change: Added extract_product_page(session, url, query=None, html=None) adapter to the catalog refresh path. It validates the ParfumZentrum product URL and reuses _extract_product with the already-fetched HTML, preserving retailer-specific size, price, availability and perfume identity checks while avoiding a second HTTP fetch.
parfumzentrum.limits: Passing CI and a read-only audit confirm the change is syntactically and operationally accepted, but do not by themselves prove that every previously failed live product URL now parses. A targeted parser fixture/live URL regression test is still required before claiming the parser_not_found issue is resolved.
